notes: Access: curl_cffi chrome131 impersonation, HTTP 200 throughout. Checked homepage mega-nav, all 11 department root pages' own sub-navs, footer, /catalog/sitemap (full tree), and static.xml -- the only 'new'-named page site-wide is /catalog/living/new-arrivals, which is also the destination of a SITEWIDE marketing banner ('Shop New Arrivals', displayOn=SITEWIDE in globalDynamicData.siteMarketingMessages), so it is treated as the site's single New Arrivals concept despite the /catalog/living/ URL prefix. Opened it and applied the Collection-page test: __NEXT_DATA__ shows documentType=EDITORIAL (breadcrumb key ED_NEW_ARRIVALS), and it is structured as 6 themed curated sub-sections (New Seating and Accent Tables, Brand New Pillows and Throws, New in Bedroom, New Dining Chairs and Banquettes, New Wall Art, New in Storage) spanning multiple departments, each with its own small productGroups array and a 'Shop More'-style button linking to a standard category page filtered by ?sort=NEWEST (e.g. /catalog/bedroom/beds?sort=NEWEST) rather than to itself. It has genuine current product tiles (86 total) but no unified browsable grid, no filter/sort UI of its own, and no site-reported count -- a magazine-style curated landing page rather than a single flat PLP. Could not conclusively determine which side of the Collection-page test it falls on, so recorded per brief guidance with a MANUAL REVIEW flag rather than including or excluding it outright. Also found and evaluated /catalog/living/new-living: documentType=EDITORIAL, single 'Fresh Ideas' set (36 tiles), generic seasonal styling copy with no New-Arrivals target-term signal (name is 'New Living', not 'New Arrivals'/'New In'/'Just Arrived' etc.) -- excluded, not a target-term match. The ?sort=NEWEST query parameter available on ordinary category pages (e.g. /catalog/living/chairs?sort=NEWEST) was also considered and excluded per brief instruction that arbitrary date/sort-filter pages on standard categories do not count as a distinct New Arrivals PLP. Site search is client-rendered (no results in SSR JSON) and a Playwright attempt hit a 'Just Checking' bot-detection challenge on /search -- first block on this host, stopped per protocol; relied on the thorough nav/sitemap discovery above instead.

rows.evidence: documentType=EDITORIAL (breadcrumb key ED_NEW_ARRIVALS); 6 themed sets in __NEXT_DATA__ props.pageProps.document.sets[]: New Seating and Accent Tables=12, Brand New Pillows and Throws=14, New in Bedroom=25, New Dining Chairs and Banquettes=8, New Wall Art=16, New in Storage=11 (86 product tiles total, no unified site-reported count)
rows.flag: MANUAL REVIEW: AMBIGUOUS NEW COLLECTION - this is the destination of the site's sitewide 'Shop New Arrivals' marketing banner, but the page itself is documentType=EDITORIAL: a curated magazine-style landing page composed of 6 themed micro-collections with 'Shop More' buttons out to filtered category pages, not one unified filterable/sortable New Arrivals grid with its own count. Contains genuine, current product tiles (86 total) representing newly added items across multiple departments, so likely reflects real new arrivals content, but could not confirm it meets the brief's bar for a genuine PLP versus an editorial/campaign landing page.
